title: Anti-frag defrag scheduler and tenant-aware spill throttle for KV cache
author: Asha Patel
description:
Context and motivation: production clusters serving bursty chat workloads were repeatedly observing elevated KV cache fragmentation which caused premature paging and aggressive spillovers under tenant contention. This manifested as 95th percentile token generation latency regressions and +20-40% extra disk spill I/O during high-concurrency experiments. Goal: reduce fragmentation-driven spill events, improve memory residency for hot prefixes, and provide a per-tenant backpressure/priority mechanism to avoid noisy-tenant tail behavior.

Summary of changes: Implement an anti-fragmentation defragmentation scheduler that coalesces adjacent free slots proactively during low-load windows and opportunistically during continuous-batching idle gaps. Introduce a tenant-priority allocator that prefers warm-run allocations for pinned tenants and gracefully demotes low-priority tenants during memory pressure. Add a spill throttle module that exposes a token-bucket-like pacing per-tenant and a global spill budget with soft quotas to avoid cascade spill storms. Feature-flagged behind kv.anti_frag_defrag and kv.spill_throttle for staged rollout.

Key behavioral changes and rationale: 1) Defrag scheduler: uses a lightweight hinting API from the allocator to identify fragmentation hotspots (small free islands). Rather than compacting aggressively, the scheduler coalesces neighbors into a small contiguous slab and updates the allocator metadata atomically to minimize stalls. This approach trades a small background CPU cost for reduced page churn and fewer writebacks. 2) Tenant-priority allocator: tenants can be assigned a steady-state priority (derived from billing tier and recent SLA). The allocator attempts in-order placement to maximize prefix locality; on pressure it lowers placement preference for low-priority tenants and exposes a graceful admission signal to the spill throttle. 3) Spill throttle: when global memory pressure exceeds thresholds, the throttle enforces per-tenant pacing and refuses immediate spillbacks that would exceed the global budget. This smooths downstream IO and reduces head-of-line eviction storms.

Perf results (canary): - Controlled canary across 10 clusters: average reduction in spill size per-minute: 28% (median); - 95th token latency improvement: 9-12% across chat workloads with sequence lengths >1024; - Tail variance reduced: observed 2x fewer spill-induced latency spikes in the canary window. Microbenchmarks show the scheduler adds ~0.7-1.5% CPU overhead during peak compaction windows but decreases overall IO wait time.

Testing and rollout: includes new unit tests, deterministic integration tests that simulate tenant contention and fragmentation, and a perf canary harness. The rollout plan is staged: feature flag off by default -> internal canary -> gradual percent rollout -> full on by default after 2 weeks of telemetry.

Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (ENG-9034) - [x] Feature flags added - [x] Unit and integration tests - [x] Perf canary passes - [x] Observability (metrics + dashboards) - [x] Docs/operational runbook updated

Operational notes and metrics added: kv.defrag.coalesces_total, kv.defrag.coalesce_latency_ms_p50/p95, kv.spill.throttle_tokens_granted, kv.tenant.allocation_priority, kv.eviction.spill_events_by_tenant. Dashboards ship under docs/operational/kv-eviction.md.

Risk and mitigations: defrag activity can cause CPU pressure; limited by windowed scheduling and guarded by a dynamic backoff. Spill throttle could introduce temporary memory oversubscription if misconfigured; default conservative budgets and an auto-fallback that disables throttle at extreme pressure.

Related work and references: builds on earlier work around soft-quarantine and spill smoothing (see ENG-8721) but differs by combining proactive coalescing with tenant-aware allocation and an explicit per-tenant spill budget.
